note: Per calibrated step, the database as it was when its labels were made: a backup beside the live database (instance/) taken before the labelled events were merged, split or rejected. `dedup_admin.py recalibrate` re-scores the labelled cases on it with the current evidence readers. A step is listed once its labels exist; each entry was checked to hold the labelled cases (event reality 162/162, duplicates 155/155, coherence 147/147, victim attribution 145/145, source gate 132/132 judgeable pages; supplier victims 139/174 - all 72 pairs, but the 33 victim candidates named only by the unstored 2026-10-27 supplier searches cannot be rebuilt); event-scope names the database to copy once its sample is labelled (scripts/calibrate_event_scope.py) and is not checked until then. Replace an entry, or pass --snapshot STEP=PATH, if the file is lost. coherence-same-organisation: cyber_events.db.backup.20261029_before_review_fixes (taken before any repair), copied to calibration_coherence_same_org.db and judged there (196 candidates). ai-duplicates names a file that does not exist until the AI pairs are labelled: after `scripts/calibrate_ai_duplicates.py score`, copy the live database to instance/calibration_ai_duplicates.db (before any AI merge is applied - merging removes the labelled pairs) and label the sampled pairs against it. victim-fill-frame-2: the second labelling frame of victim fill (scripts/calibrate_victim_fill.py, `frame` column of evaluation/victim_fill_sample.csv): the published snapshot snap-20261030181338-a80909168fd9 (sha256 a80909168fd9...), decompressed, with frame 2's scoring answers added by `score --frame 2`; calibrate with `--frame-db 2=<it>`. Frame 1 stays victim-fill. coherence-same-organisation-frame-2: the second labelling frame of the same-organisation check (scripts/calibrate_coherence_same_org.py, `frame` column of evaluation/coherence_same_org_sample.csv; frame 1 is the census-exhausted coherence-same-organisation snapshot): the published snapshot snap-20261030181338-a80909168fd9 (sha256 a80909168fd9...), decompressed, with frame 2's answers added by `score --frame 2`; calibrate with `--frame-db 2=<it>`. The frame-1 snapshot predates FinalDecisions, so `calibrate` finds no score on it until `judge` (stored answers, no calls) has run on a copy.
